# epidemia

> Bayesian semi-mechanistic modelling of infectious diseases in R. Latent daily
> infections are propagated by a discrete renewal process (self-exciting point
> process); the time-varying reproduction number R_t and observation ascertainment
> rates are modelled as (optionally multilevel) regressions; multiple observation
> series (deaths, cases, prevalence) are fit jointly. Inference is via Stan
> (CmdStanR backend). Software paper: Scott et al. (2021), arXiv:2110.12461. Applied companion: Mishra et al. (2022) JRSS-A, doi:10.1111/rssa.12988.

This file is a compact, self-contained guide for LLMs/agents that need to USE the
package. For working ON the source, see `AGENTS.md`.

## Setup (once)

```r
install.packages("cmdstanr", repos = c("https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()                 # needs a C++ toolchain
remotes::install_github("mlgh-sg/epidemia2")
library(epidemia)
# optional: epidemia::compile_epidemia()    # precompile; else compiles on first epim()
```

## Mental model: a model is 3 parts, fit by 1 function

- `epirt(formula, link, prior, prior_intercept, prior_covariance)` — the
  **transmission** model for R_t. LHS of `formula` MUST be `R(group, date)`.
- `epiinf(gen, seed_days, prior_seeds, latent, pop_adjust, pops, prior_susc, ...)` —
  the **infection** model (renewal process). `gen` = generation-time PMF (simplex).
- `epiobs(formula, i2o, family, link, prior, prior_intercept, prior_aux)` — an
  **observation** model. LHS names the observed column; RHS models the ascertainment
  rate. `i2o` = infection-to-observation delay PMF. Pass one or a `list()` of these.
- `epim(rt, inf, obs, data, algorithm, group_subset, prior_PD, ...)` — assembles and
  **fits**. Returns an `epimodel`. `...` (iter, chains, warmup, seed, cores,
  control=list(adapt_delta=, max_treedepth=)) is forwarded to the CmdStanR method.

### Data rules (important)
`data` is one long-format data frame. For each group the rows are consecutive daily
dates; the **first date is the first day of seeding** (so the observed series should
start a little after the first date — set early observations to `NA`). The `group`
and `date` columns named in `R(group, date)` must exist. Every covariate and observed
column referenced in any formula must be present.

## Minimal complete example (single region)

```r
library(epidemia); library(EpiEstim); data("Flu1918")
date <- as.Date("1918-01-01") + seq(0, along.with = c(NA, Flu1918$incidence))
data <- data.frame(city = "Baltimore", cases = c(NA, Flu1918$incidence), date = date)

rt  <- epirt(R(city, date) ~ 1 + rw(prior_scale = 0.1),   # intercept + daily random walk
             prior_intercept = normal(log(2), 0.2), link = "log")
obs <- epiobs(cases ~ 0 + offset(rep(1, 93)),             # full ascertainment (alpha = 1)
              link = "identity", i2o = rep(0.25, 4))       # infection observed over next 4 days
inf <- epiinf(gen = Flu1918$si_distr)                     # basic (deterministic) renewal

fm  <- epim(rt = rt, inf = inf, obs = obs, data = data, iter = 1500, chains = 3, seed = 12345)

summary(fm)                       # posterior quantiles + Rhat / n_eff
plot_rt(fm); plot_obs(fm, type = "cases"); plot_infections(fm)
```

## Links, families, priors

- `epirt` link: `"log"` (default), `"identity"`, or `scaled_logit(K)` to cap R_t in
  `[0, K]` (e.g. `scaled_logit(6.5)`).
- `epiobs` family: `"poisson"`, `"neg_binom"`, `"quasi_poisson"`, `"normal"`,
  `"log_normal"`. link: `"logit"` (default), `"probit"`, `"cauchit"`, `"cloglog"`,
  `"identity"`, or `scaled_logit(K)` (e.g. `scaled_logit(0.02)` to cap an IFR at 2%).
- Prior constructors provided by epidemia (identical to the same-named rstanarm
  functions): `normal()`, `student_t()`, `cauchy()`, `exponential()`, `laplace()`,
  `lasso()`, `hs()`, `hs_plus()`, `product_normal()`, `decov()`. (`lkj()` is
  exported but NOT usable as `prior_covariance` — the Stan model implements only
  `decov`, and `epirt()` rejects `lkj()` with an error.) Plus
  epidemia-specific `shifted_gamma()` (one-sided NPI effects) and `hexp()`
  (hierarchical seeding). Check the realised priors with `prior_summary(fm)`.

## Recipes

### Multilevel / partial pooling across regions
lme4 syntax in the `epirt` formula: `(expr | factor)` = correlated partial pooling
(`prior_covariance = decov(...)`); `(expr || factor)` = independent; `expr:factor` =
no pooling; plain `expr` = full pooling.
```r
rt <- epirt(
  R(country, date) ~ 0 + (1 + lockdown || country) + lockdown,
  prior = shifted_gamma(shape = 1/6, scale = 1, shift = log(1.05)/6),
  prior_covariance = decov(shape = c(2, 0.5), scale = 0.25),
  link = scaled_logit(6.5))
```
Partial pooling applies to the **R_t regression only**: `epirt()` takes
`prior_covariance`, `epiobs()` does not. For a group-varying ascertainment rate
use fixed effects (`deaths ~ 0 + country`), not `(1 | country)`.
Group-specific random walks are `rw(time = week, gr = country)`; omitting `gr`
puts every group on one shared walk.

### Multiple observation series (fit jointly)
```r
deaths <- epiobs(deaths ~ 1, i2o = inf2death, family = "poisson", link = scaled_logit(0.02))
cases  <- epiobs(cases  ~ 1 + rw(time = week), i2o = inf2case, family = "quasi_poisson")
fm <- epim(rt, inf, obs = list(deaths, cases), data = data, iter = 2000)
```

### Latent infections (over-dispersion, good for low counts)
```r
inf <- epiinf(gen = si, latent = TRUE, family = "normal", prior_aux = normal(10, 2))
```

### Population / susceptible depletion (realistic long-range forecasts)
```r
data$pop <- 56e6
inf <- epiinf(gen = si, pop_adjust = TRUE, pops = "pop", prior_susc = normal(0.9, 0.05))
# posterior_rt(fm) returns the susceptibility-ADJUSTED R_t; posterior_rt(fm, adjusted = FALSE) the raw R_t
```

### Prior predictive check (no data used)
```r
fm_prior <- epim(rt, inf, obs, data, prior_PD = TRUE, algorithm = "sampling", iter = 1000)
```

### Forecasting / counterfactuals — just pass modified `newdata`
Extend the data frame with future dates (placeholder observation values), or alter
covariates, and hand it to any posterior/plot function. No separate predict API.
```r
plot_obs(fm, type = "deaths", newdata = future_data, groups = "Italy", cumulative = TRUE)
```

### Variational Bayes for fast iteration
```r
fm <- epim(rt, inf, obs, data, algorithm = "fullrank", iter = 5e4, tol_rel_obj = 1e-3)
```

## Post-processing / extraction

- Draws of latent series: `posterior_rt()`, `posterior_infections()`,
  `posterior_infectious()`, `posterior_linpred()`, `posterior_latent()`.
- Posterior predictive of observations: `posterior_predict(fm, type = ...)`.
- Parameters: `as.matrix(fm, par_models=, par_types=, regex_pars=, par_groups=)`,
  `summary(fm)`, `prior_summary(fm)`, `posterior_sample_size(fm)`.
- Plots: `plot_rt`, `plot_obs`, `plot_infections`, `plot_infectious`, `plot_linpred`,
  and spaghetti/trajectory variants `spaghetti_rt`/`spaghetti_infections`/`spaghetti_obs`
  (args: `levels=`, `step=`, `adjusted=`, `cumulative=`, `newdata=`, `groups=`).
- Diagnostics: `plot(fm, "trace")`, `plot(fm, "areas")`, etc. (bayesplot interface).
- Forecast evaluation: `evaluate_forecast()`, `posterior_coverage()`,
  `posterior_metrics()` (CRPS / MAE), `plot_coverage()`, `plot_metrics()`.

## Bundled data

- `EuropeCovid`, `EuropeCovid2` — 11 European countries, first COVID-19 wave:
  daily cases/deaths, five NPI indicators, `si` (generation time) and
  `inf2death`.
- `EnglandB117` — SGTF-split English case counts behind Volz et al. (2021),
  *Nature* 593:266-269. 49 areas x 120 days, plus populations, the ascertainment
  rate, the delay kernel, **and the paper's own fitted estimates** (`published`,
  `published_england`) so a reproduction can check itself.
- `EnglandNewCases`, `Flu1918`.

## Delay-kernel convention (important)

Both `gen` and `i2o` are **lag-1-first**: entry 1 weights infections one day
back, and an infection is never observed on the day it happens. Entry *k* should
therefore carry the probability mass in **(k-1, k]**, i.e. `F(k) - F(k-1)`, which
puts a kernel's mean lag half a day above its distribution's mean and assigns no
mass at lag 0.

Reproductions of published work should **build their own kernel** rather than use
a bundled one: Flaxman et al. discretise at the midpoint (`F(k+1/2) - F(k-1/2)`),
which is half a day different, and the B.1.1.7 model's `i2o` sums to **7, not 1**
because its observations are weekly totals attached to a daily series.

## Random walks: read the reported parameters carefully

`R|rw(...)` draws are the walk's **increments**, not its levels — take a
cumulative sum to get the walk. Safer still, derive quantities from
`posterior_rt()` rather than from coefficients: for a two-group model the ratio
of the two groups' `R_t` cancels any shared walk and depends on no
parameterisation. (The B.1.1.7 vignette does this; reading the parameters as
levels instead gave a correlation of 0.44 with the published series where the
ratio gives 0.99.)

## Gotchas

- `epirt` LHS must be exactly `R(group, date)`; `epiobs` LHS is the observed column.
- The date column must be `Date`-coercible (not numeric).
- `i2o` and `gen` are per-day PMF vectors; `i2o` need not sum to 1 (it also encodes
  ascertainment scaling), `gen` should be a simplex.
- Set early per-group observations to `NA` so the seeding period is not treated as data.
- `NA` in an `rw(time = )` column means "this day gets no term from this walk" --
  the way to give a walk to only some groups.
- Fitting compiles Stan on first use (slow once, then cached).
- `correlated` region effects (`(1 + x | g)`, single bar) need enough groups to
  support a full covariance. With ~11 groups plus a per-group random walk it may
  not identify: check `Sigma_chol` R-hat before trusting anything downstream, and
  prefer the double-bar `||` form if it has not mixed.
```
